title: Priming architectures sketchbook
content:
Notes to self: exploring multi-stage priming patterns and lightweight scaffold templates that are robust to token budget and adversarial inputs. Goal: produce a small library of composable prompt modules (anchor, role, constraint, exemplar) that can be stitched at runtime depending on task and SLOs.

Top-level observations (quick):
- Short explicit constraints reduce hallucination in summarization tasks but sometimes make model drop important but implicit context. tradeoff = recall vs hallucination.
- Layered priming (anchor + micro-exemplar + one-line constraint) seems more robust than long single-block instructions for 2–3-shot contexts on vLLM-hosted 13B variants.
- Role toggles ("You are XYZ") can drift if examples contradict role; must align exemplars with declared role.

Experiment matrix (rough):
- Variables: anchor length (1–3 lines), scaffold depth (none | micro | full), exemplar style (contrived | natural), refusal rule presence (y/n), noise injection (random newline / fake meta).
- Targets: summarization (news), instruction-following (task lists), code transformation (JS->TS), factual QA (wiki paragraphs).

Priming module primitives (working names):
- ANCHOR: single-sentence framing + goal (eg. "Summarize the following in 2-3 bullets for a product manager.")
- ROLE: explicit persona (eg. "You are a concise product writer who avoids speculation.")
- CONSTRAINT: rules (eg. "If not in text, say 'not stated'. Max 40 words. No invented facts.")
- EXEMPLAR: 1–2 few-shot pairs (input -> target)
- SIGNAL: brief token for output format ("Bulleted" / "JSON")
- REFUSAL: explicit refusal template for hallucination prompts ("I don't have evidence to answer that from the text.")

Mini-templates (combine modules)
1) Minimal-safety summary (low cost, 1.5–3 tokens overhead)
[ANCHOR]
[CONSTRAINT_short]
[SIGNAL]
[TEXT]
-> expected: 2 bullets, no hallucination.

2) Scaffolded exemplar (higher cost)
[ROLE]
[ANCHOR]
[EXEMPLAR(1)]
[CONSTRAINT_full]
[TEXT]

3) Role-flip guard (for role-drift tasks)
[ROLE]
[EXEMPLAR contradictory]
[REFUSAL]
[TEXT]

Few-shot sets (examples):
- Summarization exemplar (natural):
IN: "ACME's Q4 revenue rose 12% driven by mobile subscriptions; margins flat due to marketing spend."
OUT: "- Revenue +12% (Q4) driven by mobile subscriptions
- Margins flat; marketing spend offset gains"

- Refusal exemplar (contrived):
IN: "Text: \"The document does not mention the CEO's age.\" Q: \"How old is the CEO?\""
OUT: "Not stated in the text."

Adversarial test cases (things that break patterns):
- Implicit knowledge asks: "What year did the company IPO?" when text only says "recently" -> model tends to guess. REFUSAL rule needed.
- Conflicting exemplars: one exemplar indicates 'avoid numbers' and the other uses numbers; model mixes styles. Fix: unify exemplar style.
- Overconstrained format + long answer: model returns prose that violates constraints. Add a final short-format signal (eg. "Output MUST be bulleted.").

Quick runs (notes from local sessions):
- 2025-02-14, model: redwood/13B-v1-qual (hosted) -> scaffolded exemplar reduced hallucination from 42%->18% on small 50-item news set, but BLEU-style overlap dropped slightly.
- 2025-02-20, model: 7B-quant -> refusal template increased correct non-answers but raised false negatives (model over-refused) ~7% more.

Failure-case log (short):
- FC1: speculative bridging when asked to infer motivation from isolated quote. Root cause: anchor too permissive ("explain"). Fix: add "only use explicit signals in text" constraint.
- FC2: token-budget slippage: when exemplar + anchor > 256 tokens, model ignores exemplar ordering. Fix: micro-exemplar (1 short pair) or move exemplar into system-level seed.
- FC3: hallucinated entity details for product names with similar tokens -> model seems to generalize brand tokens. Try adding negative examples (explicit "not present") in exemplars.

Small experiments to try next:
- Micro-exemplar placement: before vs after anchor vs inline with each paragraph. Track latency impact and output fidelity.
- Refusal softening: instead of absolute refusal, provide a template to ask for clarification "I don't have evidence; would you like a plausible hypothesis or say 'insufficient info'?" Compare business impact.
- Burst priming: feed 2 anchors with different levels of strictness and let model prefer the stricter one (test for conflict resolution).

Notes on evaluation & metrics (fast):
- Use 3 labels: correct, hallucinated, incomplete. Have simple scoring script that maps to pass/fail. Track refusal rate separately.
- Prefer precision-weighted metric for safety-sensitive tasks (precision of factual statements).

Open questions / unresolved:
- How to compute exemplar importance automatically? (attention probing? gradient saliency?)
- Is there a cheap way to encode refusal policy so that smaller models obey it as robustly as larger ones?
- What is the moment when adding examples becomes harmful (diminishing returns)? Need curve for 1–8 exemplars across models.

Operational notes:
- For hosted API runs keep anchor+exemplar under 120 tokens for 7B/quant to avoid cache thrashing.
- For Dedicated we can push bigger scaffold but still preserve short signal token at the end ("OUTPUT_START") so that downstream parsing is simpler.

Immediate TODOs (short):
- [ ] implement micro-exemplar placement ablation (Omar)
- [ ] add 100-item news dataset variant with more implicit-knowledge prompts (Priya)
- [ ] draft small Confluence page with template primitives and recommended combos (me)
- [ ] push small PR that adds refusal templates to the examples repo (PR reference above)

Random ideas (brain dump):
- Variant generator: programmatically mutate constraints (soft->hard; explicit->implicit) to create stress test bank.
- "Negative exemplar" module that shows what NOT to produce (useful for style drift).
- Lightweight verifier: after model output, run a follow-up micro-check that asks for sources/evidence from the text. If none, auto-flag.

Closing note: keep this as a messy notebook. The aim is not final rules but a composable lexicon we can A/B in Redwood Optimize. Will iterate and move cleaned templates to shared drive when stable.
